evidence: The chemical bonding information of the films was examined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS, Model AXIS, KRATOS) with a Mg Ka radiation (1253.6 eV). The phases of the films were determined by X-ray diffraction (XRD, Model M18XHF-SRA, Mac Science, Japan). The in-plane orientation and out-of-plane alignment were examined by X-ray pole figure and ω scan with θ¼0° and θ¼90° (rocking curve) (Model X’Pert Pro, PANalytical, the Netherlands). The in-plane orientation relationships between SnO2 films and sapphire substrates were further investigated by transmission electron microscope (TEM). The thickness of the deposited SnO2 films was measured by ellipsometer (Model L2W15S830, Gaertner, US) and X-ray reflectivity (XRR, Model X’Pert Pro, PANalytical, the Netherlands). The surface of SnO2 films observed by AFM were smooth, and the root-mean-square (RMS) values of the surface roughness were 1.04 and 1.48 nm (scan area 2 mm × 2 mm) for the films deposited on a- and m-cut substrates, respectively. The depth dependence of Sn and O chemical states in SnO2 films was investigated by XPS and the core level Sn3d and O1s spectra were shown in Fig. 2 as a function of the sputtering time (sputtering rate: 1 nm/min). The interfaces between films and substrates were rather well defined and atomistically sharp with a few defects. HRTEM image for the film deposited on (1 1 0) (a-cut) Al2O3, viewed along the [1 0 1¯ ] SnO2 direction (Fig. 6 (A)), exhibited the sharp (1 0 1) and (0 2 0) lattice fringes parallel and perpendicular to the interface. The FFT patterns confirmed that the (1 0 1) SnO2 film grows epitaxially on the (1 1 0) sapphire substrate with the orientation relationship of [0 1 0]SnO2//[0 0 1]Al2O3 and [1 0 1¯ ]SnO2//[1¯ 1 0]Al2O3. The HRTEM image, viewed along SnO2 [0 1 0] direction, showed the lattice fringes of (0 0 2) and (2 0 0) planes and reconirmed the above orientation relationship (Fig. 7(B)). A weak diffraction spot of SnO2 (3 0 1) plane was detected in the FFT pattern of film consistent with the X-ray diffraction (Fig. 3(B)) and pole figure (Fig. 4(B)).
